title: LEDA: a Large-Organization Email-Based Decision-Dialogue-Act Analysis Dataset
abstract: Introduces decision-focused dialogue-act annotations over real-world public IETF organizational email and studies automatic tagging of those acts. The dataset is direct evidence for decision-related communicative functions in authentic large-organization email, although it does not by itself provide the full owner, deadline, condition, and exact action-argument schema sought here.
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2023

title: Extraction de tâches dans les e-mails : une approche fondée sur les rôles sémantiques
abstract: Presents a semantic-role-based approach for detecting and structuring tasks in professional email, with roles describing who performs an action, what is done, when, and related participants. This is unusually direct evidence for structured action extraction from workplace email, although the available description does not establish joint annotation of all target slots such as conditions, exceptions, and exact evidence spans.
venue: Extraction et Gestion des Connaissances (EGC 2020)

title: On the Elicitation and Annotation of Business Activities Based on Emails
abstract: Studies discovery and annotation of business-process activities from email and extracts associated metadata such as participant roles, attachment types, and link domains. It provides direct evidence that authentic email can be structured around business activities, but the activity metadata is not equivalent to a fully annotated action-item owner/deadline/condition representation.
venue: 34th ACM/SIGAPP Symposium on Applied Computing

title: Email Business Activities Extraction and Annotation
abstract: Treats professional email as a source for recovering undocumented business activities and associated metadata useful for business-process analysis. The work is directly relevant to activity-centric structuring of workplace email, while not establishing the complete structured action benchmark required by the target gaps.
venue: Information Search, Integration, and Personalization

title: CORE - an LLM-Powered System for Resolution Mining and Retrieval from Conversational Platforms
abstract: Presents an LLM-based system that mines and structures support resolutions from enterprise conversational platforms including Slack and Microsoft Teams and makes them retrievable. It is direct enterprise-chat extraction evidence, but resolution mining is not itself a benchmark for action owner, deadline, conditionality, or decision arguments.
venue: 2026 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Data Engineering Workshops

title: Evaluating the Quality of AI-Generated Resolutions from Conversational vs Structured Sources: Implications for Enterprise Knowledge Automation
abstract: Evaluates extraction of IT-support resolutions from noisy enterprise Slack and Microsoft Teams conversations against resolutions derived from structured ticket sources. This supplies empirical evidence about structured knowledge extraction from authentic enterprise chat, but its resolution representation does not directly close the action-owner, deadline-binding, or condition-attachment gaps.
venue: NeurIPS 2025 Workshop: Reliable ML from Unreliable Data

title: Annotations for Power Relations on Email Threads
abstract: Annotates Enron email threads for organizational and situational power, influence, communication control, and utterance-level displays of power. It does not extract assignees, but it provides direct authentic-email evidence for organizational context that could be relevant when responsibility is implicit rather than named locally.
venue: Proceedings of the Eighth International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation (LREC 2012)

title: Tracing Linguistic Markers of Influence in a Large Online Organisation
abstract: Studies linguistic markers of influence in a large collaborative standards organization using a long-running IETF email archive containing organizational interactions. It does not perform action-owner extraction, but it is direct workplace-like email evidence that organizational and conversational context carries information about participant roles and influence.
venue: Proceedings of the 61st Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 2: Short Papers)

title: Building A Corporate Corpus For Threads Constitution
abstract: Describes construction and privacy-preserving processing of a corpus of real corporate email intended for conversation-thread reconstruction and analysis. The corpus is relevant to authentic workplace email and contextual reconstruction, including discussion of information such as commitments and deadlines, but it does not itself establish a structured action or decision extraction benchmark.
venue: Proceedings of the Student Research Workshop Associated with RANLP 2021

title: What Decisions Have You Made?: Automatic Decision Detection in Meeting Conversations
abstract: Studies automatic detection of decision-making dialogue acts and decision-related segments in multi-party meeting conversations using lexical, prosodic, contextual, and topical information. This is transfer evidence from meetings rather than asynchronous workplace email or enterprise chat.
venue: Human Language Technologies 2007: The Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: Automatic Decision Detection in Meeting Speech
abstract: Develops automatic detection of decision-related dialogue acts and decision segments in complete meeting transcripts. It provides transfer evidence for modeling decision discourse but does not establish structured decision extraction from email or enterprise chat.
venue: Machine Learning for Multimodal Interaction

title: Decision Detection Using Hierarchical Graphical Models
abstract: Models meeting decision subdialogues with hierarchical graphical models and distinguishes roles such as issues, resolution proposals or restatements, and agreement. This is particularly relevant transfer evidence for separating proposals and agreements around a decision proposition, although it is meeting-domain rather than email/chat evidence.
venue: Proceedings of the 48th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Short Papers

title: Focused Meeting Summarization via Unsupervised Relation Extraction
abstract: Frames decision-focused meeting summarization as relation extraction, separating decision cues from the content associated with them and identifying informative phrases from decision-related utterances. Because the underlying method explicitly relates decision indicators to decision content, it is useful transfer evidence for proposition anchoring and evidence extraction rather than merely generated summarization.
venue: Proceedings of the 13th Annual Meeting of the Special Interest Group on Discourse and Dialogue

title: Meeting Decision Tracker: Making Meeting Minutes with De-Contextualized Utterances
abstract: Presents a system that detects decision utterances in meetings and rewrites them into de-contextualized decision items for minutes. It is transfer evidence for decision detection, but generated de-contextualization is weaker evidence for exact source-span and structured-argument extraction.
venue: Proceedings of the 2nd Conference of the Asia-Pacific Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics and the 12th International Joint Conference on Natural Language Processing: System Demonstrations

title: Resolving “You” in Multi-Party Dialog
abstract: Studies whether second-person pronouns in multi-party dialogue are generic or referential and, for referential uses, identifies the intended addressee or addressees. This is transfer evidence for implicit and group participant inference; identifying an addressee must not be equated with proving that the addressee is the responsible action performer.
venue: SIGdial Workshop on Discourse and Dialogue

title: An LLM Benchmark for Addressee Recognition in Multi-modal Multi-party Dialogue
abstract: Benchmarks addressee recognition in multi-party dialogue where many turns do not explicitly identify their addressee and evaluates large language models on the task. It is transfer evidence for recovering implicit conversational participants, not direct evidence that an inferred addressee is an action owner in workplace communication.
venue: International Workshop on Spoken Dialogue Systems

title: Do LLMs suffer from Multi-Party Hangover? A Diagnostic Approach to Addressee Recognition and Response Selection in Conversations
abstract: Diagnoses large-language-model performance on addressee recognition and response selection in multi-party conversations and shows the importance of conversation structure and history. The conversations are not direct authentic workplace-email evidence, so the contribution is transfer evidence for context-dependent participant inference.
venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

title: Semantic Role Labeling of Implicit Arguments for Nominal Predicates
abstract: Studies identification of implicit semantic arguments for nominal predicates using information beyond the predicate's local syntactic environment, including preceding discourse. This is transfer evidence for recovering omitted actors or other roles, not workplace-email ownership evidence.
venue: Computational Linguistics

title: Beyond NomBank: A Study of Implicit Arguments for Nominal Predicates
abstract: Introduces and studies implicit arguments of nominal predicates that are not locally realized and demonstrates methods for finding their discourse antecedents. It is transfer evidence for implicit-role recovery relevant to omitted owners or objects.
venue: Proceedings of the 48th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: Improving Implicit Semantic Role Labeling by Predicting Semantic Frame Arguments
abstract: Improves implicit semantic-role labeling by modeling expected semantic-frame arguments and recovering roles that are not overtly expressed near a predicate. This is linguistic transfer evidence for implicit argument recovery rather than direct workplace assignee extraction.
venue: Proceedings of the Eighth International Joint Conference on Natural Language Processing

title: SemEval-2010 Task 10: Linking Events and Their Participants in Discourse
abstract: Defines a discourse-level task for linking locally uninstantiated semantic roles to participants found elsewhere in discourse. The formulation is relevant transfer evidence for owners, objects, or other action arguments recoverable only outside the local clause.
venue: Proceedings of the Workshop on Semantic Evaluations: Recent Achievements and Future Directions

title: Predicate-specific Annotations for Implicit Role Binding: Corpus Annotation, Data Analysis and Evaluation Experiments
abstract: Presents corpus annotation and evaluation for binding implicit semantic roles to non-local discourse entities for selected predicates. It supplies transfer evidence for discourse-level argument recovery, while its domain and predicates differ from workplace task ownership.
venue: Proceedings of the 10th International Conference on Computational Semantics – Short Papers

title: A Two-Step Approach for Implicit Event Argument Detection
abstract: Decomposes implicit event-argument detection into head-word identification followed by expansion to argument spans and evaluates on document-level event data. This is transfer evidence for non-local argument recovery and exact span construction, not direct workplace communication evidence.
venue: Proceedings of the 58th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: Multi-Sentence Argument Linking
abstract: Introduces the RAMS benchmark for linking event triggers to argument spans that may occur in other sentences and evaluates document-context models for the task. It is transfer evidence for cross-sentence owner, object, or time-argument recovery and precise span prediction.
venue: Proceedings of the 58th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: Entity, Relation, and Event Extraction with Contextualized Span Representations
abstract: Presents DyGIE++, a span-based architecture that jointly models entities, relations, and events with contextualized span representations and cross-sentence information. It is transfer evidence for exact trigger and argument span extraction, not a workplace action-item benchmark.
venue: Proceedings of the 2019 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing and the 9th International Joint Conference on Natural Language Processing

title: Document-Level Event Argument Extraction by Conditional Generation
abstract: Introduces a document-level event-argument extraction formulation based on conditional generation and a benchmark with document-level events, coreference, and informative argument extraction. It provides transfer mechanisms for arguments recoverable through distant context or coreference, but not workplace-domain evidence.
venue: Proceedings of the 2021 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies

title: Document-Level Event Argument Extraction by Leveraging Redundant Information and Closed Boundary Loss
abstract: Uses document-level coreference information and a closed-boundary loss to improve event-argument extraction, including argument-boundary prediction. This is transfer evidence for precise evidence spans and cross-sentence participant recovery.
venue: Proceedings of the 2022 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies

title: Document-Level Event Argument Extraction With a Chain Reasoning Paradigm
abstract: Models long-range dependencies between event triggers and arguments through explicit reasoning chains for document-level event-argument extraction. The mechanism is relevant transfer evidence for arguments located outside the sentence containing an action or decision.
venue: Proceedings of the 61st Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)

title: Document-level event argument extraction by leveraging span boundaries and argument dependencies
abstract: Develops document-level event-argument extraction using explicit span-boundary modeling together with dependencies among arguments and evaluates the approach on document-level benchmarks. It is transfer evidence for exact argument boundaries and mutually constrained argument extraction, not workplace-domain validation.
venue: Neurocomputing

title: TAGPRIME: A Unified Framework for Relational Structure Extraction
abstract: Presents a unified conditional sequence-tagging framework for relational structure extraction, including event arguments conditioned on triggers and role-related information. It is transfer evidence for extracting structured trigger-argument spans but is not an authentic workplace email/chat benchmark.
venue: Proceedings of the 61st Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)

title: Temporal Anchoring of Events for the TimeBank Corpus
abstract: Introduces annotation and modeling for anchoring events to temporal expressions in TimeBank. It is transfer evidence for learning event-to-time relations; temporal anchoring is not equivalent to determining that a date is a deadline for a workplace action.
venue: Proceedings of the 54th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: Event Time Extraction with a Decision Tree of Neural Classifiers
abstract: Models extraction of event times by decomposing temporal anchoring into neural classification decisions. It provides transfer machinery for linking events to time expressions but does not distinguish workplace deadlines from other temporal relations.
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: Event Time Extraction and Propagation via Graph Attention Networks
abstract: Represents event-time relations in a graph and propagates temporal information to events lacking explicit local time expressions. This is transfer evidence for document-level action-time association, not direct deadline semantics or deadline-to-action binding.
venue: Proceedings of the 2021 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies

title: TIMERS: Document-level Temporal Relation Extraction
abstract: Addresses document-level temporal relation extraction with models designed to use broader context when classifying temporal links. It is transfer evidence for determining which event a temporal expression relates to, but it does not supply deadline-specific workplace labels.
venue: Proceedings of the 59th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics and the 11th International Joint Conference on Natural Language Processing: Short Papers

title: DocTime: A Document-level Temporal Dependency Graph Parser
abstract: Parses document-level temporal dependencies among events and time expressions into a structured temporal graph. The method is relevant transfer evidence for disambiguating temporal attachment but does not itself identify deadline relations in workplace requests or commitments.
venue: Proceedings of the 2022 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies

title: More than Classification: A Unified Framework for Event Temporal Relation Extraction
abstract: Presents a unified framework for extracting event temporal relations rather than treating relation classification as an isolated step. It is transferable to action-time binding, but its temporal labels are not deadline-specific workplace semantics.
venue: Proceedings of the 61st Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)

title: TimeML: Robust Specification of Event and Temporal Expressions in Text
abstract: Defines TimeML representations for events, temporal expressions, and temporal links, including anchoring events to times and ordering events. It is foundational transfer work for representing action-time relations, while temporal links alone do not encode deadline semantics.
venue: AAAI Spring Symposium on New Directions in Question Answering

title: Negation Scope Refinement via Boundary Shift Loss
abstract: Targets precise negation-scope boundaries and introduces a loss designed to correct boundary errors. It is transfer evidence for exact scope-span annotation; it does not by itself attach negation to the correct workplace action when several propositions occur together.
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2023

title: Learning with Structured Representations for Negation Scope Extraction
abstract: Models negation-scope extraction with structured representations rather than independent token decisions. This is transfer evidence for scope attachment and span extraction, not direct evidence for negated workplace requests or obligations.
venue: Proceedings of the 56th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Short Papers

title: Speculation and Negation Scope Detection via Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: Detects speculation and negation cues together with their scopes using neural models. It offers transfer mechanisms for condition-like uncertainty and negation scope, but it does not evaluate attachment to action arguments in authentic workplace communication.
venue: Proceedings of the 2016 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

title: Modality and Negation in Event Extraction
abstract: Extends event extraction with explicit representation of modality and negation so extracted events can distinguish factual from modal or negated descriptions. This is transfer evidence for enriching action structures with polarity and modality, not direct workplace-email evaluation.
venue: Proceedings of the 4th Workshop on Challenges and Applications of Automated Extraction of Socio-political Events from Text

title: Agent-Specific Deontic Modality Detection in Legal Language
abstract: Introduces legal-language annotations and models for deontic modality with respect to particular agents, including modality labels and modal-trigger spans. It is strong transfer evidence for attaching obligation, permission, or related modality to the correct actor, but legal obligations are not direct workplace-conversation evidence.
venue: Proceedings of the 2022 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

title: Dialogue Act Modeling for Automatic Tagging and Recognition of Conversational Speech
abstract: Develops statistical dialogue-act modeling and automatic tagging for conversational speech using lexical, discourse-sequence, and prosodic information. It is foundational computational evidence for contextual speech-act classification and helps establish the pre-transformer lineage behind later email and workplace-dialogue act work.
venue: Computational Linguistics

title: Can Prosody Aid the Automatic Classification of Dialog Acts in Conversational Speech?
abstract: Investigates automatic dialogue-act classification in conversational speech and the contribution of prosodic information alongside other evidence. It is foundational transfer literature from the 1990s rather than direct workplace email extraction evidence.
venue: Language and Speech
